caption:
Swipe through. SpaceX just launched NASA's Roman telescope nine months early, with a spy mirror aboard and 1.35 million names heading to deep space. 🔭

Roman launched on Falcon Heavy Aug 30, nine months ahead of schedule and on budget, mirror originally built for U.S. intelligence agencies but the same size as Hubble's at less than a quarter of the weight, 1,350,144 names aboard heading to L2, each image covering 100 times more sky than Hubble, both side boosters landing simultaneously for SpaceX's 13th straight Falcon Heavy success, and all survey data dropping public after processing.

NASA just proved flagship missions don't have to run late. Spy satellite hardware became the most powerful public astronomy tool ever launched. Five years, 50 times Hubble's sky coverage, all free.

Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.

Sources: NASA, SpaceX

pinned_comment: The center booster wasn't recovered on purpose. Roman was heavy enough that SpaceX needed full thrust from all three cores, so the center was planned to be expended from the start.
